syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

book.title: Exploring Society India and Beyond Part-II
book.edition: NCERT (reprint year not stated in the prelims)

topics.title: Mapping the Earth: projections and physical maps
topics.ncert_sections: The Complexity of Mapping the Earth

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why every map projection of the Earth shows some distortion.
Compare what the Mercator and Robinson projections preserve and distort.
Identify the landforms and water bodies shown by each colour on a physical map.

topics.title: The oceans of the blue planet
topics.ncert_sections: The Blue of the Blue Planet, the Oceans; Ocean currents; Ocean trenches

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how oceans cover the Earth, support life and regulate climate.
Explain how warm and cold ocean currents affect the climate of coastal areas.
Describe ocean trenches such as the Mariana Trench and how life survives there.

topics.title: Coral reefs and smaller water bodies
topics.ncert_sections: The Great Barrier Reef; Smaller water bodies and waterways

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why coral reefs such as the Great Barrier Reef matter and what threatens them.
Distinguish seas, gulfs, bays, straits and canals and their role in trade.

topics.title: Asia: Tibetan Plateau, Gobi, Steppes and Urals
topics.ncert_sections: Asia

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the formation and importance of the Tibetan Plateau, the 'Third Pole'.
Describe the Gobi Desert and the Eurasian Steppes and their role in nature.
Explain the importance of the Ural Mountains and the tundra and taiga around them.

topics.title: Europe and Africa: plains, the Alps, deserts and the Nile
topics.ncert_sections: Europe; Africa

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the European Plain and the Alps support agriculture, water supply and settlement.
Describe the Sahara Desert and the African savannah and how life adapts to them.
Explain the importance of the River Nile for people in Africa.

topics.title: The Americas: Andes, Amazon, Atacama and North American landforms
topics.ncert_sections: South America; North America

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the Andes and the Amazon and why they are important for the planet.
Describe the Atacama Desert and the environmental problem it faces.
Describe the Colorado Plateau, the Rockies, the Appalachians and the Great Lakes.

topics.title: Australia, cold deserts and caring for the Earth
topics.ncert_sections: The Australian Continent; Before we move on

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the Great Australian Desert, its wildlife and its people.
Recognise that deserts can be cold, with Antarctica as the largest desert on Earth.
Evaluate how human actions disturb natural features and why sustainable use is needed.

topics.title: Crown Rule and the Royal Proclamation of 1858
topics.ncert_sections: A Royal Proclamation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how India was governed after 1858 and why the proclamation's promises were not kept.
Identify the forms of racial discrimination and repressive laws Indians faced under colonial rule.

topics.title: Reform Movements and Other Influences
topics.ncert_sections: Reform Movements; Other Influences

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the founders, places and key ideas of the major 19th-century reform movements.
Describe how Bankim Chandra's Anandamath and Bande Mataram fed nationalist feeling.
Explain Swami Vivekananda's ideas on self-confidence, science and India's spiritual roots.

topics.title: The Rise of the Congress and Growing Discontent
topics.ncert_sections: The Rise of the Indian National Congress; Growing Discontent

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the founding of the Indian National Congress and the aims of its early phase.
Explain the reforms and anti-colonial methods of the Kuka (Namdhari) Movement.
Describe the resistance led by Tilak, the Chapekar brothers and Birsa Munda.

topics.title: The 1905 Partition of Bengal and the Nationalist Agenda
topics.ncert_sections: The 1905 Partition of Bengal and National Awakening; The Nationalist Agenda; The All-India Muslim League; The 1907 Surat Split

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the real motive behind the 1905 partition of Bengal and the popular response to it.
Explain the Swadeshi, boycott and National Education programmes and the demand for Swaraj.
Distinguish between the Moderates and the Nationalists and explain the 1907 Surat split.

topics.title: The Revolutionaries, Home Rule and the Lucknow Pact
topics.ncert_sections: The Revolutionaries; Home Rule Movement and the Lucknow Pact

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the main revolutionary actions from the Alipore Bomb Case to the Ghadar Movement.
Explain the aims of the Home Rule Movement and the terms of the Lucknow Pact of 1916.

topics.title: Gandhi, Non-Cooperation, Jallianwala Bagh and Khilafat
topics.ncert_sections: Gandhi and the Non-Cooperation Movement; The Jallianwala Bagh Massacre and its Aftermath; The Khilafat Movement and its Aftermath

concepts.learning_objective: Explain Gandhi's method of satyagraha and the course of the Non-Cooperation Movement.
Describe the Jallianwala Bagh massacre and its impact on Indian opinion.
Evaluate the aims, support and consequences of the Khilafat Movement.

topics.title: Protests, Purna Swaraj and Civil Disobedience
topics.ncert_sections: Protests, Repression and Revenge; Purna Swaraj and Civil Disobedience; The Gandhi-Irwin Pact; The Idea of Separate Nations

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the protests against the Simon Commission and the revolutionary actions that followed.
Explain the Purna Swaraj resolution and how the Salt March launched Civil Disobedience.
Describe the Poona Pact and the rise of the idea of separate nations.

topics.title: World War II, Quit India, Partition and Independence
topics.ncert_sections: World War II and the Indian National Army; The Quit India Movement; Partition, Turmoil, and Independence

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the impact of World War II on India and the role of Subhas Chandra Bose's INA.
Describe the Quit India Movement and why it worried the British.
Explain the events leading to Partition and the factors behind Britain's exit from India.

topics.title: Harappan Urban Architecture

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the planned streets, drains and fortified areas of Harappan cities such as Mohenjo-daro and Dholavira.
Explain why Harappan builders chose bricks or stone depending on what was locally available.

topics.title: Stupas and Rock-Cut Architecture

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the form and features of stupas such as those at Sanchi and Bharhut and how the Buddha was represented.
Explain how rock-cut caves such as Udayagiri-Khandagiri and Ellora were carved and used.

topics.title: Water Structures

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how Harappan wells, Shringaverpur's reservoirs and other structures harvested and stored water.
Describe the engineering, artistic and social role of stepwells and temple tanks.

topics.title: Classical Temple Architecture

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the main elements of a classical temple such as the gopuram, mandapa, garbhagriha and shikhara or vimana.
Explain the temple as a representation of Purusha and worship as a journey from the outer to the inner world.
Compare regional temples such as Brihadishvara, Lingaraja, Dilwara and Bishnupur by builder and material.

topics.title: The Architecture of Mosques

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the main features of a mosque such as the prayer hall facing Mecca, domes, minarets and the mihrab.
Explain how Indo-Islamic architecture blended Islamic building traditions with Indian craftsmanship.

topics.title: Forts and Palaces

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why forts were located strategically and how they were planned and supplied.
Describe palaces such as those at Agra, Orchha and Mysuru and the styles they reflect.

topics.title: Tombs and Mausoleums

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish mausoleums from cenotaphs and explain why tombs belong mainly to faiths that bury the dead.
Describe the features of Humayun's Tomb and the Taj Mahal and the cultures they blend.

topics.title: Traditional Houses, Churches and Colonial Architecture

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the central-courtyard design of havelis and Chettinadu houses and what they reveal about their owners.
Describe how churches in India, especially in Kerala, adopted local architectural traditions.
Identify Indo-Saracenic architecture as a colonial style blending Islamic, Hindu and Gothic elements.

chapters.title: The Role of the Judiciary in Our Society

topics.title: Justice, Law and the Role of the Judiciary
topics.ncert_sections: Introduction; The Connection Between Law and Justice

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the judiciary ensures fair adjudication and keeps laws and executive action within the Constitution.
Define laws as general rules made by the government that carry consequences when they are not followed.
Identify examples of unjust laws in India and elsewhere and explain why they were repealed.

topics.title: Substantive and Procedural Justice
topics.ncert_sections: The Connection Between Law and Justice (aspects of justice)

concepts.learning_objective: Describe substantive justice as concern with whether the final decision is fair, just and reasonable.
Explain procedural justice as a full hearing for every party and the presumption of innocence.

topics.title: The Judicial System and the Supreme Court of India
topics.ncert_sections: The Judicial System in India; The Supreme Court of India

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the unified hierarchy of courts with the Supreme Court at the apex, High Courts and District Courts.
Recall when and under which Article the Supreme Court was established and its role as final interpreter.
State how Supreme Court judges are appointed, their qualifications, strength and retirement age.

topics.title: Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court
topics.ncert_sections: Writ Jurisdiction; Public Interest Litigation; Original, Appellate and Advisory Jurisdiction; Special Leave Petitions

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how citizens can enforce Fundamental Rights through writ petitions under Articles 32 and 226.
Explain how Public Interest Litigation lets people raise issues of public concern before the courts.
Distinguish the original, appellate, advisory and special leave jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.

topics.title: High Courts, Subordinate Courts and Tribunals
topics.ncert_sections: High Court; Jurisdiction of the High Courts; Subordinate Courts; Tribunals

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the appointment, qualifications, retirement and writ and supervisory powers of High Courts.
Explain the place of subordinate courts in the judicial system and how District Judges are appointed.
Identify specialised tribunals and the categories of disputes each one decides.

topics.title: New Criminal Laws and Digital Technology in the Judicial System
topics.ncert_sections: Digital Technology and Judicial System; Digital Initiatives

concepts.learning_objective: Match the colonial-era criminal laws with the new laws of 2023 that replaced them.
Explain how digital initiatives make the judicial system more accessible and transparent.

topics.title: Alternate Modes of Dispute Resolution
topics.ncert_sections: Alternate Modes of Dispute Resolution

concepts.learning_objective: Describe arbitration and how a binding award differs from other modes of settlement.
Explain mediation as assisted mutual settlement in which the mediator imposes no decision.
Describe the purpose and legal basis of Lok Adalats and Gram Nyayalayas.

topics.title: Who Is a Citizen?

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish a citizen, who legally belongs to a country, from a resident who only lives there.
Explain citizenship as both a legal identity and a social responsibility involving active participation.
Identify the laws that set the rules for gaining or losing Indian citizenship.

topics.title: What Are Rights? Fundamental Rights and the Right to Equality

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why only claims that support the wellbeing and dignity of all count as rights.
Identify the six categories of Fundamental Rights and that they can be enforced in courts.
Distinguish equality from equity and relate the right to equality to non-discrimination.

topics.title: Right to Freedom, Right to Life and Right against Exploitation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the right to freedom comes with reasonable restrictions.
Describe the right to life as the right to live with dignity, including livelihood, health and a clean environment.
Apply the protections against child labour, forced labour and trafficking to real situations.

topics.title: Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights and Constitutional Remedies

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the freedom to choose, practise and share religion and the neutrality of state-run schools.
Describe how cultural and educational rights protect minorities' language, script and institutions.
Evaluate why the right to constitutional remedies is called the heart and soul of the Constitution.

topics.title: Duties: Fundamental Duties and Their Link with Rights

concepts.learning_objective: Recall when and how Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution.
Identify the Fundamental Duties in Article 51A from everyday examples.
Explain why rights and duties are two sides of the same coin and how they differ in enforcement.

topics.title: Discrimination

concepts.learning_objective: Define discrimination and explain how it harms individuals and society.
Distinguish visible from invisible discrimination and explain why the latter is hard to penalise.
Recognise how Savitribai Phule and Anandibai Joshi fought discrimination.

topics.title: Inclusion

concepts.learning_objective: Explain inclusion as making everyone feel welcomed, respected and given equal access.
Suggest practical steps that remove barriers to participation in school and society.

topics.title: What Is Demography?
topics.ncert_sections: What Is Demography?; Don't Miss Out (census)

concepts.learning_objective: Define demography as the study of the size, structure and composition of a population and how it changes over time.
Explain how governments and businesses use demographic information to plan services and allocate resources.
Describe the census as the official count of a country's people and the information it collects.

topics.title: Population at a Glance: India and the World
topics.ncert_sections: Population at a Glance

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the growth of world population since 1950 and the UN projection of its peak and decline.
State India's position as the most populous country and its share of the world population.
Explain how medical advances and better sanitation caused rapid population growth after the 1950s.

topics.title: Birth Rate and Fertility Rate
topics.ncert_sections: What Determines the Population of a Country?; Birth and fertility rates

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish between birth rate and fertility rate and how each affects population growth.
Explain the replacement level fertility rate of 2.1 and what happens above and below it.
Analyse why fertility rates fall, using China's One-Child Policy and the role of girls' education and urbanisation.

topics.title: Mortality Rate and Migration
topics.ncert_sections: Death or mortality rate; Migration

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret mortality rate, child mortality and life expectancy as indicators of health and well-being.
Explain the causes of migration and its effects on the areas people move to and from.

topics.title: Stages of Demographic Transition
topics.ncert_sections: How Do Countries Experience Population Change?

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the three stages of demographic transition in terms of birth and death rates.
Relate phases of India's population history to the stages of demographic transition.

topics.title: India's Population: Composition, Sex Ratio and Pyramids
topics.ncert_sections: India's Population: Composition and Trends; Improvement in India's sex ratio

concepts.learning_objective: Define sex ratio and interpret India's sex ratio figures from the Census.
Interpret the shape of a population structure diagram and how India's pyramid has changed since 1950.

topics.title: Demographic Dividend and Population Ageing
topics.ncert_sections: India's Demographic Dividend - A Limited Window of Opportunity

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the demographic dividend and youth bulge and why India's window of opportunity is limited.
Analyse the challenges of an ageing population and the ways nations prepare for it.

topics.title: Urban and rural areas, and population density
topics.ncert_sections: Introduction; Population Density in Cities

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish urban areas from rural areas by population, occupations, infrastructure and local governing bodies.
Calculate and compare population density as the number of people per square kilometre.

topics.title: How cities become centres of economic activity
topics.ncert_sections: How do Cities Become Centres of Economic Activities?; What Leads to Urbanisation?

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how location near rivers, coasts, trade routes or raw materials helps a place grow into a city, as in Jamshedpur.
Describe urbanisation and the stages by which a rural area turns into a metropolitan area.

topics.title: Economic hubs and specialised cities
topics.ncert_sections: Mumbai, Bengaluru, smaller urban centres, Agra, Varanasi and Delhi

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how institutions, clusters of industries and education helped cities like Mumbai and Bengaluru become hubs.
Identify smaller urban centres known for particular industries and why firms locate in growing cities.
Analyse how historical, cultural and pilgrimage sites drive economic activity and livelihoods in cities.

topics.title: Cities as cultural hubs
topics.ncert_sections: Cities as Cultural Hubs

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how cities mix cultures, food and festivals, using examples such as vada pav and Kolkata's Durga Puja.
Describe how cultural centres, museums, libraries and stadiums help city residents interact and form networks.

topics.title: Challenges faced by cities
topics.ncert_sections: Challenges Faced by Cities

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the pressures that growing populations put on city infrastructure, air quality and safety.
Explain why slums grow in cities, how slum dwellers support the city, and how housing schemes respond.
Evaluate how collective action revived Bengaluru's lakes and eased its water crisis.

topics.title: Planning our cities: the Pink City of Jaipur
topics.ncert_sections: Planning Our Cities; India's 'Pink City'

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the factors urban planners must consider, such as jobs, transport, land use and public safety.
Describe the planning features of Jaipur and how they suited security, trade, aesthetics and the dry climate.

topics.title: Dynamic urban planning of Singapore
topics.ncert_sections: Dynamic urban planning of Singapore

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how Singapore's Concept Plan and Master Plan make its long-term planning flexible.
Analyse how mixed-use spaces, public transport and vertical gardens give dense Singapore a good quality of life.

topics.title: Urban redevelopment and sustainable cities of tomorrow
topics.ncert_sections: Urban redevelopment in India; concluding section

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Indian redevelopment projects such as the Sabarmati Riverfront and Gangtok's M.G. Road.
Evaluate how technology and sustainable planning can balance city growth with care for people and Nature.

topics.title: Belief systems and the power of the bhakti tradition
topics.ncert_sections: Belief Systems; The power of the bhakti tradition; Regional saints and their messages

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the bhakti marga as a path to moksha and why it united people during political instability.
Identify bhakti saints of different regions and the messages of equality and oneness they spread.
Recognise the common patterns of continuity, patronage and participation seen in the 13th to 17th centuries.

topics.title: Sufism and its meeting with bhakti
topics.ncert_sections: Sufism

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Sufism as a devotional path of Islam and the role of music such as qawwali in it.
Explain how Bhakti and Sufi traditions overlapped, including the work of Dara Shikoh.

topics.title: Musical traditions: continuation and evolution
topics.ncert_sections: Musical Traditions - Continuation and Evolution

concepts.learning_objective: Describe regional storytelling traditions such as puppetry and pattachitra.
Distinguish the Hindustani and Carnatic streams and the growth of dhrupad.
Explain how instruments like the sitar and tabla evolved while drawing on older Indian traditions.

topics.title: Miniature paintings and gardens
topics.ncert_sections: From Walls to Paper - Miniature Paintings; Changing Landscapes - Gardens

concepts.learning_objective: Compare Rajput and Mughal miniature painting and the exchanges between them.
Describe the charbagh design of Mughal gardens and how later gardens borrowed from it.

topics.title: Women in society: contextual variations in role and status
topics.ncert_sections: Women in Society - Contextual Variations in Their Role and Status

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why practices like purdah spread in some regions and not in others.
Identify the roles of women such as Razia Sultan and Nur Jahan in governance.
Interpret evidence of women's roles in public life in south India, especially Vijayanagara.

topics.title: Education, knowledge traditions and vocational learning
topics.ncert_sections: Education and Knowledge Traditions; Institutions of learning; Vocational education and knowledge sharing

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the institutions of learning of the period, from gurukulas and mathas to madrasas.
Explain why decentralised systems of learning survived political turmoil.
Describe how textile skills were passed on and enriched, as in Banarasi saris and pashmina shawls.

topics.title: Growth of literature and language
topics.ncert_sections: Growth of Literature and Language; The development of Urdu

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the growth of literature in regional languages under bhakti saints and royal patrons.
Identify translations between Sanskrit and Persian and their role in preserving knowledge.
Explain how Urdu and Dakhini developed by blending Indian and Persian-Arabic elements.

topics.title: Science, architecture and cultural exchange in daily life
topics.ncert_sections: Developments in Science and Technology; Regional Architectural Developments; Cultural Exchange in Daily Life

concepts.learning_objective: Identify advances in mathematics, astronomy and applied chemistry made in this period.
Explain how temple building and reconstruction showed cultural resilience.
Distinguish adoption from adaptation of foreign influences in food and clothing.
